necessary_context.content: [n]={1,...,n}; a batch is a multiset of S indices, sampled with replacement, and B_batch(x)=S^{-1} sum_i B_i(x). Section 2 updates V^k=V^{k-1}+B_batch(x^k)-B_batch(x^{k-1}), using the same batch at both points. Its initial estimator V^0 is supplied, rather than constructed by this component.

necessary_context.content: Eq.(2.7) states E||B_i(x)-B_i(y)||^2 <= L_B^2||x-y||^2. The adjacent text requires ||x^k-x^{k-1}|| <= epsilon_1 for k=1,...,K. Lemma 1 Eq.(2.8) gives initial MSE plus k L_B^2 epsilon_1^2/S.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.8, Eq.(2.7), surrounding text and Lemma 1 Eq.(2.8)
necessary_context.name: Mean-square Lipschitz condition and bounded path increments

necessary_context.content: Eq.(2.6) prints E[B_i(x^k)-B_i(x^{k-1}) | x_{0:k}] = V^k-V^{k-1}. Appendix A defines E_k as conditioning on x_{0:k}; A.2 centers increments using B(x^k)-B(x^{k-1}) and invokes a martingale decomposition. Conditioning only on a point sequence does not by itself establish orthogonality to the complete past estimator error for an arbitrary adaptive process. The submitted fresh-batch formulation explicitly supplies full-history predictability and independent batches; those are local sufficient conditions, not a verbatim quotation of Eq.(2.6).
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.8 Eq.(2.6); p.25 Appendix A introduction, A.1 and A.2 Eq.(A.2); p.26 Eq.(A.3)–(A.5)
